claim: Closing the window saves prefs and destroys the app.

suggested_fix: Fit the image into the box keeping the aspect ratio (PIL ImageOps.contain) and render with scale × DPI factor.
what: thumbnail rendered at 2x the box and sized to fit it with the page's aspect ratio

claim: Single source of the app version, shown in the title bar (app.py:63) and sidebar footer (app.py:233).
why_wrong: The release is 3.2.2 (version_info.txt FileVersion '3.2.2.0', folder name v3_2_2) and setup.py:8 says '3.2.1'. Users and bug reports see v3.0.0, and the three sources disagree.

what: theme.__version__ = '3.2.2'
note: HANDOFF (docs lane): setup.py:8 version '3.2.1' -> '3.2.2' (or read paperknife/theme.py); README.md:1 says 3.2.1; version_info.txt, installer.nsi:18 and build_windows.bat:21 already say 3.2.2 but are hand-kept copies.

quote: # Always call through _tk_color() so they respond to mode changes.
claim: Using _tk_color makes native widgets respond to mode changes.
why_wrong: _tk_color returns one string at widget creation (line 63); an existing tk.Listbox/Canvas keeps it after ctk.set_appearance_mode. It only looks correct because every navigation rebuilds the view.
suggested_fix: Say 'resolves the colour for the current mode at call time; rebuild native widgets after a mode change'.
what: comment now says _tk_color resolves at call time and native widgets must be rebuilt after a mode change

claim: Comment 28 lists WCAG AA passes (dark values verified: 10.94, 5.57, 5.35, 3.05, 14.62, all as stated).
why_wrong: The AA check covered only the dark palette. In light mode MUTED on SIDEBAR (#7A7268 on #EDE8DF), used for the status bar (12px, app.py:262-265), section headers (9px bold) and the job label, measures 3.88:1, below the 4.5:1 AA minimum for normal text.

note: Light-mode MUTED #7A7268 on SIDEBAR is 3.88:1 (below AA 4.5:1 for the 12px status bar and 9px headers): darken it to about #6A635A?

claim: Theme constant.
why_wrong: Grep 'GREEN' over paperknife: only this line. It duplicates SUCCESS (line 45, same hex).
suggested_fix: Delete it.
what: unused GREEN constant deleted (grep: only its definition)

quote: "Settings are saved automatically and persist between sessions")
claim: Settings are saved automatically.
why_wrong: Nothing is saved until the user clicks 'Save Preferences' (_save, line 81). Edits are lost if the user navigates away, because show() rebuilds _vars from PREFS.
suggested_fix: Change the subtitle to 'Click Save to keep changes', or save on change.
what: subtitle now 'Click Save Preferences to keep changes'

claim: Max recent files shown accepts a number.
why_wrong: No range check: 0 or a negative number is saved as is. recent.py:62 `self._entries[:_max_recent()]` then wipes the history on the next file open. Measured: max_recent=0 -> entries [] and recent.json '[]'; -1 -> 0 entries. Non-numeric input silently becomes 12 with no message (bare except). The same applies to default_dpi (line 92-93): 0 or a negative value is accepted and becomes the Batch DPI default.
suggested_fix: Clamp max_recent to 1..50 and DPI to 72..600, and tell the user when input is rejected.
what: max_recent must be 1..50 and default_dpi 72..600; non-numeric or out-of-range input shows a warning and nothing is saved; _max_recent() also floors at 1

claim: The Colour mode menu shows the current preference (light/dark/system).
why_wrong: get_appearance_mode() returns the resolved 'Light'/'Dark', never 'System' (measured: set 'system' -> 'Dark'). A user who chose 'system' sees 'dark', and the next Save of any setting writes appearance='dark', silently turning off following the OS theme.
suggested_fix: Initialise from PREFS.appearance instead.
what: Colour mode row reads PREFS.appearance (keeps 'system') instead of ctk.get_appearance_mode()

quote: if not messagebox.askyesno("Restore", "Reset all preferences to defaults?"):
claim: Restore resets all preferences to defaults.
why_wrong: _restore only rewrites the on-screen fields and persists only appearance (lines 111-113). output_dir, max_recent, DPI, compress level and OCR language stay unchanged on disk unless the user also clicks Save; if they navigate away, the mode is reset but nothing else is. window_geometry is never reset.
suggested_fix: Copy _DEFAULTS into PREFS._data (keeping window_geometry if wanted), save, and re-render.
what: Restore copies _DEFAULTS (except window_geometry) into PREFS, applies the mode, saves, and re-renders the view

claim: Default values.
why_wrong: This duplicates prefs._DEFAULTS (prefs.py:12-21) by hand, so the two can drift apart. They match today.
suggested_fix: Import _DEFAULTS from prefs.
what: Restore uses prefs._DEFAULTS instead of a hand copy

claim: Watermark tool stamps a diagonal text watermark across every page (subtitle 'Stamp a diagonal text watermark across every page', enhance.py:117).
why_wrong: PyMuPDF Page.insert_text only accepts rotate in {0,90,180,270}. Probe (l2_probe.py, PyMuPDF 1.28.2): page.insert_text(..., rotate=45, render_mode=0) -> 'RAISES ValueError: bad rotate value'. The worker raises on page 1 of every document, so the Watermark tool never produces output; the user only sees an error dialog.
suggested_fix: Use insert_text(..., morph=(pivot, fitz.Matrix(45))) or insert_textbox/TextWriter with a morph matrix instead of rotate=45.
what: New watermark_pdf(): insert_text with morph=(centre, Matrix(45 + page.rotation)) in unrotated page space, font shrunk so the 45-degree line fits inside the page; centred, diagonal on rotated pages too (checked 0/90/180/270 by render).

claim: Batch 'Watermark' operation applies a watermark to every PDF in the folder.
why_wrong: Same rotate=45 call as the single tool; probe shows 'ValueError: bad rotate value' for every page, so every file in a batch watermark run ends as '✗ <name> — bad rotate value' (and the final status is then overwritten with a green 'Done', see L2 run_job finding).
suggested_fix: Share one fixed watermark helper (morph matrix) between WatermarkTool and batch.
what: Batch _do_watermark calls the shared enhance.watermark_pdf (same code as the tool).

claim: The Opacity slider (5-100%, label '25%') controls watermark transparency.
why_wrong: opacity is computed and never passed anywhere (ruff F841 confirms); the insert_text call at enhance.py:200-205 has no fill_opacity/stroke_opacity argument, so the watermark would be 100% opaque regardless of the slider. UI control whose value is never read.
suggested_fix: Pass fill_opacity=opacity (and stroke_opacity) to the text insertion call.
what: Opacity slider value passed as fill_opacity/stroke_opacity (ExtGState /ca equals the slider).

claim: Batch Watermark 'Opacity:' option (batch.py:173) is applied to each file.
why_wrong: Value read then never used (ruff F841); insert_text at batch.py:49-50 has no opacity argument and a hard-coded grey colour, so the batch option is ignored and output differs from the single tool's colour choice (parity gap).
suggested_fix: Pass fill_opacity=opacity; expose colour or document it is fixed grey.
what: Batch opacity option now reaches watermark_pdf; colour stays the fixed grey (0.5,0.5,0.5), which is the single tool's default; batch has no colour control.
note: Batch has no colour option; adding one would be a new control (not done).

claim: Medium/Aggressive compression 'resample images' (labels at enhance.py:35-40, subtitle 'Reduce file size by cleaning streams and downsampling images'); Medium is the default level (prefs.py:15 compress_level 'medium').
why_wrong: Code at enhance.py:68-86 rasterises EVERY WHOLE PAGE to a JPEG and builds a new image-only PDF: all text, vectors, links, bookmarks, forms and annotations are destroyed. Probe on a 20-page text PDF: orig 7 KB -> 767 KB, extracted text after = '' . The default compress setting therefore makes text PDFs ~100x larger and unsearchable.
suggested_fix: Resample only embedded images (page.get_images / replace_image) and keep page content; or relabel as 'Rasterise pages (destroys text)' and stop making it the default.
what: Medium/Aggressive no longer rasterise pages: compress_pdf() calls Document.rewrite_images with bicubic subsampling to exactly 150/96 DPI (images above that DPI only), JPEG q80, then garbage=4/clean/deflate save. Text, vectors, links stay.
note: rewrite_images' built-in path uses FZ_SUBSAMPLE_AVERAGE (integer factors: 360 DPI lands at 180 not 150), so PdfImageRewriterOptions is built directly with FZ_SUBSAMPLE_BICUBIC; recompress_when=WHEN_SMALLER. Needs PyMuPDF with rewrite_images (1.28.2 in venv; requirements.txt still says >=1.23 - outside my lane).

claim: Completion dialog reports '(N% smaller)' / status '(−N%)'.
why_wrong: When output grows (the common case for rasterised text PDFs) pct is negative; probe computed pct_label = -10857, so the status reads '7 KB → 767 KB (−-10857%)' and the dialog says '-10857% smaller'. Also no fallback keeps the original when the result is larger.
suggested_fix: If new >= orig, say 'larger by X%' (or keep the original and warn).
what: Saving computed from bytes, original size read before the save; when the output is not smaller the status is a WARN and a warning dialog says so instead of '% smaller'.
baseline_fail: AssertionError: ... Original: 6 KB  →  New: 715 KB  (-11816% smaller)
note: Output is still written when larger (the user chose the path); no keep-original fallback added.

claim: PDF/A-1b/2b/3b conversion; 'PyMuPDF ≥ 1.24 supports pdfa= parameter' (pdftools.py:92).
why_wrong: Document.save in PyMuPDF 1.28.2 has no pdfa parameter (probe: inspect.signature lists no 'pdfa'; save(pdfa=1) -> 'TypeError: unexpected keyword argument pdfa'). Every PDF/A run takes the except branch, saves an ordinary PDF and tells the user 'Full PDF/A conversion requires PyMuPDF ≥ 1.24 ... Upgrade' while 1.28 is installed. The tool can never produce PDF/A.
suggested_fix: Remove the PDF/A option (or implement it with a real converter such as Ghostscript/ocrmypdf) and delete the false version message.
what: PDF/A option, its level selector and the false 'requires PyMuPDF >= 1.24, upgrade' message removed; PDF Tools now offers Repair only. Verified: Document.save/write in 1.28.2 raise TypeError 'unexpected keyword argument pdfa'.
note: Owner question: do you want a real PDF/A path (e.g. Ghostscript -dPDFA or ocrmypdf as an optional external tool)? PyMuPDF 1.28 cannot produce PDF/A.

claim: 'Embeds all fonts, sets colour profile. Required for long-term archiving' (pdftools.py:27-28).
why_wrong: No code embeds fonts, adds an OutputIntent/ICC profile or XMP PDF/A metadata (grep for OutputIntent/icc/xmp in pdftools.py: 0 hits); see the pdfa= TypeError finding — output is a plain PDF.
suggested_fix: Drop the claim with the option.
what: The PDF/A-1b claim ('Embeds all fonts, sets colour profile') went with the option; subtitle now 'Repair corrupt files'.

claim: 'Linearise — Optimise for fast web / browser viewing' (pdftools.py:29-31).
why_wrong: Probe: save(linear=True) on PyMuPDF 1.28.2 -> 'FzErrorArgument: code=4: Linearisation is no longer supported'. The Linearise option always fails with an error dialog.
suggested_fix: Remove the option or linearise via qpdf (--linearize).
what: Linearise option removed. Verified: save(linear=True) on 1.28.2 raises FzErrorArgument 'Linearisation is no longer supported'.
note: Owner question: want linearisation via an external qpdf --linearize? Not possible in PyMuPDF 1.28.

claim: Batch 'OCR' produces '<name>_ocr.pdf' with a searchable text layer (parity with the OCR tool, MANUAL 5.6 'invisible text layer ... searchable').
why_wrong: insert_htmlbox with color:transparent emits no text at all. Probe: same call -> extractable text '' ; with color:black -> 'HELLO'. Batch OCR output is an image-only JPEG PDF with no text, i.e. it makes files LESS searchable. ocr.py:179 uses render_mode=3 (invisible) instead — batch does not share that code.
suggested_fix: Reuse ocr.py's per-word insert_text(render_mode=3) path in batch.
what: Batch OCR writes the text layer as invisible words (render_mode=3) at Tesseract word boxes from image_to_data, the same approach as the OCR tool, instead of insert_htmlbox color:transparent (which writes no text).
note: Implemented locally in batch.py (image_to_data rather than ocr.py's hOCR regex). Possible later share with ocr.py (lane FE) - not required for correctness. Also fixed in passing: BatchTool._op_changed raised UnboundLocalError for OCR because a function-local 'from ..prefs import PREFS' shadowed the module import (test_batch_ocr_options_pane_builds; baseline: UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'PREFS').

claim: Scale mode 'Stretch (fill page)' (enhance.py:264).
why_wrong: show_pdf_page defaults keep_proportion=True, and the call at enhance.py:308 does not pass keep_proportion=False. Probe: a 200x800 red page shown into the full A4 rect -> left-edge pixel (255,255,255) white, centre red, i.e. letterboxed exactly like Fit. Stretch is identical to Fit.
suggested_fix: Pass keep_proportion=False when stretch is selected.
what: show_pdf_page(..., keep_proportion=not stretch) so Stretch fills the target page.

claim: Split extracts the requested page range.
why_wrong: Ranges that start past the end are not rejected: '7-9' on a 5-page file gives (6,4); probe insert_pdf(from=6,to=4) -> 1 page, page 5, saved as '<base>_part01_p7-5.pdf'. Reversed ranges '5-3' give pages ['5','4','3'] in reverse (probe), unlike Merge which silently drops reversed ranges.
suggested_fix: Validate 1<=a<=b<=total and report invalid parts instead of clamping.
what: Split parses ranges with the new shared paperknife.pages.parse_ranges, which rejects ranges past the end and reversed ranges with a message before the output folder is asked; nothing is written on error

claim: Single page numbers are extracted as typed.
why_wrong: Single pages are not clamped or validated: '99' on a 5-page file -> probe insert_pdf(98,98) returns page ['5']; file is named '..._p99-99.pdf' but contains page 5. '0' gives p=-1 -> the last page too.
suggested_fix: Reject p<0 or p>=total with a message.
what: single pages go through parse_ranges: '99' -> 'page 99 does not exist (the document has 5 page(s))', '0' -> 'pages start at 1'

quote: a, b = [int(x) for x in part.split("-")]
claim: Page-range syntax is the same across tools (Merge/Crop/Header placeholders offer '8-end').
why_wrong: Split does not accept 'end' (int('end') -> ValueError shown as raw 'invalid literal for int()'), nor tolerates an empty part '1,,3'. Merge, Crop and Header/Footer accept 'end'.
suggested_fix: Use one shared parser.
what: Split accepts 'end' and tolerates empty parts ('1,,3') via the shared parser; bad tokens get a readable message instead of int() errors
baseline_fail: AssertionError: [('showerror', 'Split Error', "invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'end'")]
note: HANDOFF for the coordinator: two parsers outside lane FC still exist and silently clamp/drop: paperknife/tools/crop.py:110-119 and paperknife/tools/headerfooter.py:148-158. Replace each with: from ..pages import PageRangeError, parse_ranges; pages = [p for a, b in parse_ranges(range_str, total) for p in range(a, b + 1)] if range_str else list(range(total)); catch PageRangeError and showerror before writing. merge.py and split.py now use parse_ranges; merge.py's private _parse_range is deleted.

claim: Per-file page range '1-3, 5, 8-end' selects pages; 'leave blank to include all pages'.
why_wrong: Reversed range '5-3' yields range(4,3) = [] and out-of-range pages are filtered at line 24 without any message; if every file's range is empty/out of range the merged doc has 0 pages and merged.save (line 180) fails: probe 'ValueError: cannot save with zero pages'. A typo silently drops a file's pages from the merge.
suggested_fix: Report invalid/empty ranges per file before merging.
what: every file's range is parsed with parse_ranges on the Tk thread before the save dialog; a reversed/out-of-range/garbage range shows '<file name>: <reason>' and nothing is merged (zero-page save can no longer happen)

claim: Range placeholder 'all  or  1-5, 8, 10-end'.
why_wrong: No .lower() (unlike merge.py:18 and crop.py:113), so '10-End' or 'END' raises ValueError and aborts the whole run.
suggested_fix: Shared parser with case-insensitive 'end'.
what: Header/Footer uses the shared parser (paperknife/pages.parse_ranges via crop.selected_pages), case-insensitive 'end', duplicates removed, bad input -> error dialog before any write.
baseline_fail: AssertionError: [('showerror', 'Error', "invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'End'")]

claim: One page-range grammar.
why_wrong: Four divergent hand-rolled parsers: merge.py:12-24 (lower, drops reversed), split.py:56-63 (no 'end', clamps, reverses), crop.py:112-119 and headerfooter.py:151-159 (no lower). Same input gives different pages per tool; see the individual findings.
suggested_fix: Move _parse_range to a util module with validation and use it everywhere.
what: crop.py and headerfooter.py both use FC's paperknife/pages.parse_ranges through one small helper crop.selected_pages (blank/'all' = every page, sorted unique). Overlapping ranges no longer crop twice / stamp twice.
note: merge.py and split.py are other lanes' files (not touched).

claim: Clicking a file name selects that file for Up/Down/Remove.
why_wrong: idx is frozen at creation. After '↑/↓' (line 125 swaps self._entries) or '✕ Remove' (line 140 pops), the button still selects its ORIGINAL position. E.g. add A,B,C; remove A; click B -> _select(1) highlights and targets C; pressing Remove (or Delete key, _cur_del_fn) removes C, not B.
suggested_fix: Bind the entry dict, and look up its current index at click time.
what: name button closes over its entry dict and looks up self._entries.index(entry) at click time

quote: entries = [(title, page - 1) for level, title, page, *_ in self._toc
claim: Split at each bookmark into chapter files.
why_wrong: get_toc reports page -1 for bookmarks without a page destination; start becomes -2. The previous chapter's end becomes -3 so it is skipped by 'if start > end: continue' (line 107-108) and dropped, and the -1 entry gets insert_pdf(-2, end); probe insert_pdf(from=-2,to=1) -> pages ['1','2'] (from the document start). Entries are also not sorted by page, so with 'All bookmark levels' any out-of-order bookmark silently drops sections.
suggested_fix: Filter page<1 entries and sort by start page before computing ends; report skipped entries.
what: entries with page outside 1..len(doc) (get_toc's -1) are dropped and counted, the rest are sorted by start page before ends are computed; the Done message says how many were skipped
baseline_fail: AssertionError: {'02_Loose.pdf': ['Page 1', 'Page 2'], '03_B.pdf': ['Page 3', 'Page 4']} (chapter A dropped); and {'01_A.pdf': ['Page 1', 'Page 2'], '03_A1.pdf': ['Page 2', 'Page 3']} (A2 dropped, page 2 duplicated)
note: Output file numbers now count the kept entries (01_A, 02_B) rather than the raw TOC index.

claim: Save PDF writes the edited bookmarks.
why_wrong: The input is held open in self._doc. If the user saves over the input file (natural for a bookmark editor) PyMuPDF refuses: probe 'ValueError: save to original must be incremental'. No same-path check in app._save_as (app.py:616-622). Same failure for every tool that keeps src open while saving (crop, header/footer, password, pdftools, watermark).
suggested_fix: If out == src use saveIncr()/save to temp then os.replace after close.
what: when the chosen output is the open input (os.path.samefile) the TOC editor uses doc.saveIncr(), otherwise save(deflate=True) as before
baseline_fail: AssertionError: [('showerror', 'Error', 'save to original must be incremental')]
note: HANDOFF: the finding says the same save-over-input failure exists in crop.py, headerfooter.py, password.py, pdftools.py and watermark.py (src held open while saving to out); the same pattern applies there (saveIncr when samefile, or save to a temp file, close src, os.replace).

claim: Delete removes one bookmark.
why_wrong: Deleting a parent leaves its children with a level jump; set_toc then raises at save: probe set_toc([[1,'A',1],[3,'B',2]]) -> 'ValueError: bad hierarchy level in row 1'. Nothing validates levels on Add/Update either (level list 1-4 at line 43).
suggested_fix: Promote children on delete and validate hierarchy before save.
what: Delete promotes the removed entry's descendants one level; Save checks the hierarchy (each row at most one level deeper than the previous, first row level 1) and warns with the row number and title instead of set_toc's 'bad hierarchy level' error
baseline_fail: AssertionError: [('showerror', 'Error', 'hierarchy level of item 0 must be 1')]

claim: Bookmark page number is stored as entered.
why_wrong: No range check against page count; probe set_toc([[1,'A',99]]) on 5 pages silently stores page 5.
suggested_fix: Validate 1<=pg<=len(doc).
what: Add/Update share _read_fields, which requires an open PDF and 1 <= page <= len(doc)

claim: Document lifecycle.
why_wrong: show() runs on every navigation (tool_base.py:56) and resets self._doc without closing the previously opened document; the file handle stays open (Windows lock) until GC. Same in rotate.py:50.
suggested_fix: Close any existing self._doc at the top of show().
what: show() closes any document still held from the previous visit before resetting self._doc
baseline_fail: AttributeError: 'BookmarksTool' object has no attribute '_doc' (baseline Bookmarks held no doc; the Toc/Rotate part of the test is the regression check)

claim: Opening a new PDF replaces the current one.
why_wrong: The old doc is closed BEFORE the new open (line 66); if fitz.open fails the function returns with self._doc still pointing at the closed document. Next Save/rotate: 'if not self._doc' calls len() on a closed Document -> ValueError 'document closed'.
suggested_fix: Open the new doc first, then close the old one; or set self._doc=None in the except.
what: _open opens the new file (via app._open_pdf_safe) first and closes the old document only on success

claim: Thumbnails preview the page and its rotation.
why_wrong: Every thumbnail is forced to 100x130, so landscape pages and pages rotated 90/270 are squashed into portrait; the preview of a rotation looks distorted. Also _render (line 86-92) rasterises every page synchronously on the Tk thread on each click, freezing on large files.
suggested_fix: Size CTkImage from pix.width/height; render lazily or in a worker.
what: thumbnails are sized from the pixmap to fit 100x130 keeping aspect (landscape and 90/270 rotations no longer squashed) and cached per (page, rotation), so a rotate or move re-rasterises only the changed page
baseline_fail: AttributeError: 'RotateTool' object has no attribute '_thumb' (low severity; no baseline proof attempted)
note: The first render after Open is still synchronous on the Tk thread; moving it to a worker was left alone as a larger change.

claim: 'Top/Left/Right/Bottom' margins cut those visible edges.
why_wrong: cropbox is in unrotated coordinates; on a page with /Rotate 90 'Top' cuts a visual side. Probe: Top=100 on a rotated A4 page changed visible rect from 842x595 to 742x595 (width shrank, height unchanged).
suggested_fix: Map margins through page.rotation (or page.derotation_matrix) before building the rect.
what: Margins are applied to the page as seen (page.rect) and mapped into the unrotated crop box with page.derotation_matrix plus the crop-box origin; checked for /Rotate 0/90/180/270 with an offset crop box.

claim: Status reports how many pages were cropped.
why_wrong: Pages whose new rect is empty are skipped at line 131-132 ('continue') but still counted in len(pages); also negative margins raise 'ValueError: CropBox not in MediaBox' (probe) and abort the whole run with no per-page explanation.
suggested_fix: Count applied pages; validate margins against each page size first.
what: Negative margins refused up front with a warning; only pages actually cropped are counted, skipped pages named in a WARN status.

quote: ctk.CTkCheckBox(card, text="Reset to original crop box first (undo previous crops)",
claim: Reset restores the original crop box.
why_wrong: Line 125 uses page.set_cropbox(page.mediabox): it resets to the MediaBox, discarding an original CropBox that differed from the MediaBox (e.g. printer marks).
suggested_fix: Relabel 'Reset to full media box'.
what: Checkbox relabelled 'Reset to full media box first (undo previous crops)' - what set_cropbox(page.mediabox) really does.

claim: Size and Margin fields control the stamp.
why_wrong: Any non-numeric value in either field silently replaces BOTH with defaults (no warning), unlike Crop which warns.
suggested_fix: Warn on invalid input.
what: Non-numeric Size/Margin now shows a warning and stops, like Crop, instead of silently using 10/20.

claim: n/a
why_wrong: Assigned and never read (ruff F841); centre is the else branch at line 182.
suggested_fix: Delete the line.
what: Dead is_center assignment deleted.

claim: Checkboxes 'Allow printing' / 'Allow copying text' set what the recipient may do.
why_wrong: Starting from 0 silently REVOKES every other right: high-quality print (PDF_PERM_PRINT_HQ), accessibility extraction (screen readers), form filling, annotating, assembling. Probe with both boxes ticked: HQ bit False, accessibility bit False. 'Allow printing' therefore yields degraded low-res printing only.
suggested_fix: Start from PDF_PERM_ACCESSIBILITY|PRINT_HQ|FORM|ANNOTATE etc. and clear only the unticked rights.
what: Permissions start from all eight rights (_ALL_PERMS); unticking 'Allow printing' clears PRINT and PRINT_HQ, unticking 'Allow copying text' clears COPY only.

claim: Owner password 'defaults to same'; permission checkboxes restrict the recipient.
why_wrong: With owner == user, anyone who can open the file authenticates as owner: probe authenticate('u') -> 6 (owner rights), so the print/copy restrictions are ineffective in the default flow and the user is not told.
suggested_fix: Generate a random owner password when the field is blank, or warn that restrictions need a distinct owner password.
what: Blank owner password now becomes a random secrets.token_urlsafe(24) owner password, so the open password gives user rights only and the print/copy restrictions hold; placeholder changed from 'Owner password (defaults to same)' to 'Owner password (blank = random)'.
note: Done on coordinator instruction (makes the Allow-printing/copying checkboxes' promise true). Placeholder wording changed accordingly; owner may want different wording.

claim: Remove Password requires the current password.
why_wrong: For a PDF with only an owner password, MuPDF auto-authenticates the empty user password so is_encrypted is False; probe: owner-only file -> is_encrypted False, saved unencrypted, permissions -4 (all restrictions stripped) without entering anything. A non-encrypted input also reports 'Unlocked PDF saved'.
suggested_fix: Require owner authentication (authenticate()==owner) to strip restrictions, or say so; tell the user when the file was not encrypted.
what: No change.
note: Owner question: should Remove Password refuse to strip restrictions from an owner-password-only PDF unless the owner password is entered (authenticate()==owner), and say 'this file was not encrypted' for plain inputs, instead of silently saving an unrestricted copy?

claim: Add / Change Password works on an existing protected PDF (title 'Add / Change Password').
why_wrong: An encrypted input is never authenticated, so save raises; probe: 'ValueError: document closed or encrypted'. 'Change' is impossible without first using Remove.
suggested_fix: Authenticate with the current-password field before re-encrypting.
what: Protect on an already-encrypted input authenticates with the 'Current password' field first; wrong/blank password gives a clear error instead of 'document closed or encrypted'.

claim: '# Re-open with repair flag' (line 77).
